newsitem.title: INDIA: India seen remaining as biggest gold user.
newsitem.headline: India seen remaining as biggest gold user.

text.p: India will remain the world's largest gold consumer, underpinned by rising rural prosperity and an historic affinity with the metal, a top gold analyst said on Friday.

India's position as a leader in gold consumption was bolstered by rural buying, George Milling-Stanley, manager of gold market analysis at the World Gold Council (WGC), told a two-day economic conference on gold in New Delhi.
"The research that the council is doing suggests that large purchases of gold are done by the rural population," Milling-Stanley told Reuters later.
Milling-Stanley said India's middle classes had shifted to buying gold more for adornment -- as in developed countries -- than for saving.
"Developing countries are accounting for more and more demand every year. They are stepping up the pace and will continue to outpace the developed world," he said.
"This is partly because of thousands of years of affinity with gold. There is a real understanding of the value of gold in this part of the world," Milling-Stanley said.
He said India, with annual gold consumption of about 500 tonnes, was already ahead of other developing countries.

India lifted a ban on gold imports in 1990 and has gradually liberalised the gold sector, allowing expatriate Indians to bring in up to five kg (11 lb) of gold once every six months, subject to a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grams (0.3 ounces).
"The whole notion that gold is not good for the Indian economy is finally laid to rest," Milling-Stanley said.
India's gold holdings are estimated at 9,016 tonnes, mainly accumulations from centuries of trading, and account for about 7.0 percent of an estimated world stock of 128,800 tonnes.
Most of India's gold holdings consist of family heirlooms and dowry items acquired over many years.
India produces just about two tonnes annually against an estimated annual demand of 400 tonnes.
According to WGC, India's gold demand in the first three quarters of 1996 was estimated at 365 tonnes, up from 360.4 tonnes in the same period in the previous year.
Gold is a form of security for people in rural areas where 70 percent of India's 900 million population lives. It is also used as a hedge against inflation.
